subject: Re: Acme Corp - Rerank model fit validation (post-call recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — rerank model fit

Hi Emma / team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Call highlights:
- Business goal: improve search relevance for product catalog queries (primary KPI: NDCG@10; secondary: MRR).
- Current pipeline: BM25 + TF-IDF candidate retrieval, then a lightweight reranker.
- Pain: precision drop on long-tail queries and observed regressions after some model updates.

Our hypotheses / initial recommendations:
1) Try a neural reranker (bi-encoder + cross-encoder hybrid) tuned for your latency SLO (target P95 latency < 120ms on dedicated pool).
2) Use prefix KV caching and a small candidate-rescore approach to keep token-costs down.
3) Evaluate on your labeled holdout with NDCG and MRR slices (long-tail, brand queries, multilingual).

Needed from you to validate model fit:
- A sample holdout (~5k labeled queries + candidate lists) or a pointer to a secure Drive dataset.
- Any guardrails (query types to exclude, PII redaction requirements).

Attachments: acme-rerank-benchmark-specs.pdf — I attached a short spec for the benchmark we discussed (metrics, slice definitions, suggested A/B plan).

Next steps (proposed):
- Emma to share dataset link and timeline (we discussed a 2-week validation cadence).
- Aditya/Neha: start drafting an evaluation plan and an A/B rollout canary (traffic split, monitoring hooks, regression thresholds).
- We'll run a quick model-fit run and return an NDCG/MRR summary + recommended model variant within 7 business days after we get the data.

If that sounds good, we'll go ahead and schedule the first validation run as soon as you share the data.

Thanks!

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — initial eval plan & model recs

Thanks Emma / Marissa — copying Rishi for product constraints. Quick technical plan from SE side: 

1) Model recommendations (based on latency/cost target):
- Option A (balanced): small cross-encoder (7B quantized) for top-50 candidate rescoring. Expected NDCG lift: ~6-10% on our internal retail benchmarks with P95 latency ~90ms on a 1-GPU Dedicated pod.
- Option B (higher quality): medium cross-encoder (13B with q4h) for top-20 rescoring. Expected NDCG lift: ~10-14% but higher cost; P95 ~140-160ms (we can use autoscale & canary to control spend).
- Option C (cheap / incremental): improve feature weighting + lightweight neural re-ranker (bi-encoder) with online calibration. Low cost, small NDCG lift (~2-4%) but very safe.

2) Validation artifacts we'll produce:
- rerank-ndcg-summary.csv (attached): NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, latency percentiles per model variant + slice breakdowns.
- Prompt sets / query templates we used (will include edge-case prompts for brand and long-tail).
- A/B plan template (linked): rollout steps, monitoring hooks (NDCG, MRR, error rate, latency, token-cost), automatic rollback thresholds.

3) A/B plan (proposal):
- Week 0: run offline validation on holdout and share rerank-ndcg-summary.
- Week 1: Canary with 5% traffic, monitor NDCG/MRR delta and error/latency for 48-72h.
- Week 2: Ramp to 25% if no regressions; full rollout after monitoring window and legal sign-off.

Attachments: rerank-ndcg-summary.csv (CSV, 12KB) — initial simulated numbers (placeholder until we run on ACME holdout).

I'll queue the first model-fit run once we have access to the Drive dataset and confirmation on PII handling.

—Aditya

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — question on prompt sets & regression thresholds

Quick follow-up from the DS side — thanks for the plan. A couple of clarifying Qs that will affect our evaluation: 

1) Prompt sets: can we confirm whether the holdout includes the exact user-facing query text (no internal expansions)? We'll want to run both raw queries and normalized variants. Please confirm in the Drive metadata.

2) Regression guardrails: what's an acceptable NDCG drop for slices? From prior work we recommend: no more than 0.5% overall NDCG drop; for critical slices (brand, high-funnel) we usually set a 0.2% tolerance. For MRR we recommend similar relative thresholds (0.5-1% depending on slice).

3) Slice coverage: request explicit labels for 'brand', 'navigational', 'long-tail', and 'multi-lingual' where possible. If labels aren't present we can auto-derive but want to note that will add noise.

I'll prepare a short eval checklist (test harness, metric calculation, alert thresholds) and share it once dataset access is confirmed.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Staff Data Scientist | Redwood Inference
